summary:
[trial 1]: BTC sits at $95K on 2026-04-26, only 5.3% below the $100K threshold with 8 months remaining. Base-rate barrier-crossing math under 50% annualized vol and zero drift gives ~85–90% probability of touching $100K at some point; I shade this down to ~73% to account for negative post-halving cycle drift (the halving was 24 months ago, past the typical 12–18 month peak window) and tail risk of a sustained macro-driven drawdown that suppresses a recovery rally. The dominant bull case is that BTC's high intra-period volatility makes a 5% relief rally extremely likely even in a broadly bearish regime. The main failure mode is a hard macro landing that drags BTC to $60–75K and keeps it there through year-end.

[trial 2]: BTC closed at $95,000 on 2026-04-26, requiring only a 5.3% gain to breach $100K at any daily close before year-end. With ~8 months remaining and BTC's historical ~60% annualized volatility, a naive random-walk model puts the touch probability near 0.91. However, three discounts bring this down: (1) $100K is a psychologically sticky resistance level and BTC has been consolidating nearby rather than breaking through; (2) post-ATH macro risk — if a risk-off episode drives BTC to $65–70K territory, recovery within the year is plausible but not assured; (3) the target requires a daily close, not just an intraday spike. Bull supports include strong structural institutional demand (spot ETF inflows), a short distance to target, and an 8-month window that is long by crypto standards. Balancing these, estimated probability is 0.72.
